newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Gasunie eyes gas sales to eastern Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Gasunie eyes gas sales to eastern Europe.

text.p: Dutch gas producer Nederlandse Gasunie is stepping up efforts to sell gas to eastern Europe and a possible first move into the Czech Republic looks promising, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.
"We are talking to the Czech Republic and it looks promising, but the deal is far from certain," said Gasunie spokesman Abraham Warner.
Warner said the deal could be clinched within the next two weeks and would involve sales of 1-2 billion cubic metres of gas per year over 10 to 15 years.
Gasunie, owned 50 percent by the Dutch state and 25 percent each by Royal Dutch/Shell and Exxon Corp unit Esso, also hopes to interest other eastern European nations, including Slovakia and Poland.
"We are furthest down the line with the Czech Republic, but we know of interest from Poland and Slovakia," Warner said.
Slovak President Michal Kovac, on a state visit to the Netherlands this week, will visit Gasunie's headquarters in Groningen on Wednesday afternoon.
"That points to their interest in the gas business," said Warner.
In September, Dutch Minister of Economic Affairs Hans Wijers granted Gasunie permission to increase its export contracts by 240 billion cubic metres (bcm) and imports by 120 bcm.
The Czechs rely on Russia for their gas supply, but should begin taking Norwegian gas from January.
Last week, during a visit by Dutch Minister of Foreign Trade Anneke van Dok-van Weele, the Czech Industry and Trade Ministry said it was reviewing four options for diversifying supplies.
A source at the ministry said one of the options involved purchases from Gasunie.
